mcq.q: An embedded system performs physical computing using:
mcq.e: Input (sensors), process (processor running firmware), output (actuators).

mcq.q: The instructions that tell an embedded processor what to do are called:
mcq.e: Firmware is stored in ROM and does not change at run time.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the four main constraints named in the lecture?
mcq.e: The four are cost, weight/size, power consumption and real-time performance.

mcq.q: In an anti-lock braking system the actuator is:
mcq.e: The pump releases fluid to a wheel that is braked less than the others.

mcq.q: The main reason industry shifted from hard-wired electronics to embedded software is that software is:
o: Easier to implement, cheaper, easier to debug and modify
mcq.e: Generic hardware plus software gives flexibility and lower cost.

mcq.q: A microprocessor-based implementation is also called a:
mcq.e: Separate chips on one board. A microcontroller is the single chip computer.

mcq.q: Why is an adaptive traffic control camera system usually microprocessor-based?
o: Image processing needs lots of RAM and processing power and there is no power or size limit
mcq.e: A fire alarm, by contrast, is microcontroller-based.

mcq.q: Why is ROM (Flash) larger than RAM in a microcontroller?
o: ROM stores bulky firmware while RAM stores only a few variables
RAM is more expensive to make small
mcq.e: ATmega328P: 32 KB Flash against 2 KB RAM.

mcq.q: Which memory keeps settings that must survive power loss but can be changed by the program?
o: ROM written by the developer only
mcq.e: EEPROM is non-volatile and rewritable at run time (1 KB on the ATmega328P).

mcq.q: The ADC is needed because:
o: Real-world signals are mostly analog but the processor understands only digital
mcq.e: It converts voltages from sensors into numbers.

mcq.q: PWM is used to:
o: Give an analog-like output (for example dim an LED) by digital means
mcq.e: The duty cycle sets the average output.

mcq.q: Compared with SPI, I2C is:
o: The same speed with one wire
mcq.e: SPI is fast with four wires; I2C (TWI) is slower with two.

mcq.q: Which serial peripheral is used for microcontroller-to-PC communication?
mcq.e: Universal Synchronous Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter.

mcq.q: Logic level of a pin pulled up to 5 V through a resistor with an open switch:
mcq.e: Pressing the switch connects the pin to ground, giving 0.

mcq.q: The file produced by the compiler and uploaded to the microcontroller's ROM is the:
mcq.e: Hexadecimal machine code.

mcq.q: Why is an 8-bit microcontroller ideal for academic purposes?
o: It is easier to learn and cheaper, with free tools
mcq.e: You can migrate to 32-bit later.

mcq.q: AVR microcontrollers are made by:
mcq.e: PIC is also Microchip; 8051 is Intel; STM8 is STMicroelectronics.

mcq.q: The ATmega328P has how many I/O pins on three ports?
mcq.e: Ports B, C and D give 23 I/O pins in the 28-pin package.

mcq.q: ATmega328P program memory is:
mcq.e: 32 KB Flash (16-bit word addressable).

mcq.q: On an Arduino Uno, the built-in LED is on digital pin 13 which is:
mcq.e: Arduino pins 8 to 13 are PB0 to PB5.

mcq.q: Which Arduino pins support PWM?
mcq.e: Marked with a tilde (~) on the board.

mcq.q: Why must sensors not be wired to Arduino pins 0 and 1?
o: They are the serial Rx/Tx pins used for USB communication
mcq.e: Connections there interfere with uploading and serial communication.

mcq.q: Why must a bare-metal firmware contain an endless loop?
o: There is no OS to take control back, so after the last instruction the CPU would run into garbage
mcq.e: Peer notes: with no OS execution is line by line, so loop forever.

mcq.q: The ATmega328P architecture is:
mcq.e: Separate program and data memory; mostly single-cycle instructions.

mcq.q: The recommended maximum clock of the ATmega328P is:
mcq.e: The Arduino Uno runs it at 16 MHz.

written.q: Define an embedded system, name its three functional blocks and list four constraints. Illustrate with an example.
written.a: An embedded system is a computer system embedded into another system to perform a dedicated task. It performs physical computing with sensors (capture the state of the physical world), a processor (executes firmware) and actuators (change the physical world). Constraints: cost, weight/size, power consumption, real-time performance. Example: ABS. Speed sensors measure wheel rotation; the processor compares the four wheels; a hydraulic pump (actuator) releases brake fluid to a wheel braked more than the others until all rotate at the same speed.

written.q: Compare microprocessor-based and microcontroller-based implementations and justify the choice for (a) an adaptive traffic control camera and (b) a fire alarm.
written.a: Microprocessor-based: separate CPU, ROM, RAM, I/O on a board (single board computer); high performance, replaceable parts, but expensive, power hungry, hot and bulky. Microcontroller-based: everything in one chip (single chip computer); cheap, low power, compact, but parts cannot be replaced and performance is modest. (a) Traffic camera: image processing needs a lot of RAM and speed and there is no size or power limit, so a microprocessor board. (b) Fire alarm: binary sensors, tiny processing, battery power, small and bought in bulk, so a microcontroller.

written.q: Explain the function of the core components of a microcontroller.
written.a: CPU executes instructions; ROM/Flash stores firmware; RAM stores variables; EEPROM stores non-volatile settings; ADC converts analog sensor voltages to numbers; oscillator provides precise clock pulses; PWM produces analog-like outputs; timers measure time and count events; I/O ports connect sensors and actuators; serial interfaces (USART, SPI, I2C) communicate with other devices; RESET restarts execution from the first instruction.

written.q: Explain how a program written on a PC ends up running on an ATmega328P, and why ATmega328P / Arduino Uno is chosen for learning.
written.a: The source (C or assembly) is compiled/assembled to a HEX file, which a programmer or the Arduino bootloader (via AVRDUDE) uploads into the Flash ROM. The CPU then fetches and executes the instructions. The ATmega328P is an 8-bit AVR (easy to learn, cheap, free tools), the most popular and best documented MCU, and the heart of the Arduino Uno, the most used development board. It has 32 KB Flash, 2 KB RAM, 1 KB EEPROM, 23 I/O pins, 3 timers, 6 PWM channels, 10-bit ADC, USART, SPI and I2C, in a breadboard-friendly 28-pin PDIP.
